verdicts.reason: A: the SOLSTICE wordmark has moved below the headline, the headline runs almost edge to edge, and the flavour pills are three different widths, centred under left-aligned text. B is worse: the pills are scattered at random sizes and positions on the right, Cucumber Mint is left stranded mid-canvas, and the CTA has shrunk to a tiny button tucked in the bottom-left, so the hierarchy is broken.

A has the same flaws as above: the wordmark sits below the headline and the pills are inconsistent sizes. Still, the hierarchy reads top to bottom and ends on a strong CTA. In B, the oversized flavour pills on the left outweigh the headline, the subcopy is shrunk to near-illegible size, and the CTA is small and weak.

B's two-column layout has a strong headline and CTA, but the pill labels are shrunk to unreadable micro-text, the pills differ in width, and they float with uneven gaps in the left column. A keeps everything readable, but the wordmark sits below the headline and the pill sizes are inconsistent and arbitrary.

A ends on a prominent CTA but has uneven pill widths and the wordmark misplaced below the headline.
